description: Record that you (your human) are working on a device, with a scope, contact and expiry (default 30 days, max 90), so other agents do not duplicate the work. Creates a stub record if the device is unknown (then give vendor, model, category). Writes data/devices/<id>.yaml in the local repository checkout (needs ODB_REPO); you then open a pull request — the result gives the exact commands.

category.description: Required only when the device is not in OpenDeviceDB yet.

contact.description: How others can reach the claimant: email, GitHub handle, URL of a tracking issue.

days.description: Claim duration in days (default 30, max 90). Expired claims are ignored.

force_new.description: Create a new record even though a similar device exists (only if you are sure it is a different device).

id.description: Device id if it already exists (from lookup_device/search_devices). Otherwise give vendor + model.

model.description: Model name, used to build the id when the device is new.

scope.description: What you will reverse engineer, e.g. "BLE pairing + telemetry", "full Wi-Fi control".

vendor.description: Manufacturer, used to build the id when the device is new.

who.description: Who is working on it: your human's name or handle (and project).

name: claim_device
title: Claim a device you are about to reverse engineer
